key_insight: LaMo learns a self-supervised prior over frame-to-frame latent motion directly from the unlabeled videos used to train video diffusion models, and uses that latent motion prior to bias generation toward physically consistent dynamics.
problem_solved: Addresses the gap of physical and motion inconsistency in modern video generators without relying on external simulators, teacher models, or curated physics data.
method: Formulate a latent motion prior over frame-to-frame changes in the model's latent space, capturing typical dynamic patterns.
Train the prior self-supervised on the same unlabeled video corpus used for diffusion training (extracting motion cues from latent transitions).
Integrate the learned prior into video diffusion sampling or finetuning to nudge generations toward more physically plausible and temporally consistent motions.
impact: Provides a plug-in, data-efficient way to improve physical realism in generative video systems, reducing dependence on curated physics datasets or external simulators and enabling more reliable world simulation and downstream applications.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: video frames → latent encoder → latent motion prior (learned) → diffusion generator, showing where the prior is applied

paper_title: LaMo: Self-Supervised Latent Motion Priors for Physical Realism in Video Generation
paper_authors: Bo Jiang, Depu Meng, Yihan Hu, Yichen Xie, Tianshuo Xu
